n: A temple-entrance psalm: worshippers ask, “Lord, who may stay in your tent and live on your holy hill?” The answer lists qualities of character, not ritual.

f.w: who shall abide in thy tabernacle?

f.g: Mount Zion, where God’s sanctuary stood.

n: The one whose life is blameless, who does what is right, and who speaks truth from the heart.

f.g: Lives with integrity, whole and blameless.

f.w: speaketh the truth in his heart

n: Who doesn’t slander, doesn’t harm a neighbor, and doesn’t spread gossip about friends.

f.g: Slanders, speaks evil of someone behind their back.

n: Who rejects the contemptible but honors those who revere the Lord, and keeps a promise even when it costs him.

f.w: sweareth to his own hurt, and changeth not
f.g: Keeps his word even when it hurts him.

n: Who doesn’t charge interest to exploit the poor or take bribes against the innocent. Such a person will never be shaken.

f.g: Interest on a loan; Israel’s law forbade charging interest to a needy fellow Israelite.
Accepts a bribe to pervert justice.
